top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Chile's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.
72ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
5,099ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At Gran Fondo Chile, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Chile. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 70 miles.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Chile. Train it until it feels boring.
70 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
5,099ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,099ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work supports 5,099ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.

race_overlay.weather: October in Lago Ranco, Los Rios, Chile. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Gran Fondo Chile. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan for Gran Fondo Chile's 70 miles. Start early and use products you tolerate. The organizer has not published a reliable resupply plan, so rehearse a self-sufficient carry and revise it when the rider document is released.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Gran Fondo Chile. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, TT Threshold, and VO2max to prepare you for 70 miles of mixed terrain in Lago Ranco, Los Rios, Chile.
